subject: Tenant eviction & sandboxing architecture: evidence package and diagrams
messages:
From: Samuel Park <sam.park@oakridgehealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: security@oakridgehealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant isolation / eviction procedures — initial evidence request

Irene,

Thanks for taking this. Oakridge is finalizing the vendor security review and we need a concise package describing how Redwood handles tenant sandboxing and tenant eviction for Dedicated/Private deployments. Specifically, our auditors want:

- An architecture diagram that shows how control plane, serving plane, and customer VPCs are logically segregated (we need callouts for egress control points).
- A playbook that describes the sequence when a tenant is evicted or suspended (who initiates, what data is quarantined, log retention, time to full traffic cut).
- A sample of audit/audit-log output showing eviction events (redacted).

Can you provide something we can include in our SOC 2 / SIG package? Delivery by EOD Tue 17 Aug would be ideal.

Best,
Samuel Park
IT Security Manager
Oakridge Health

Attachment: none (requesting evidence)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <sam.park@oakridgehealth.com>
Cc: k arthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / eviction procedures — initial evidence request

Samuel — thanks, we can do that. High-level plan and owners:

- Architecture diagram (control-plane vs serving-plane vs customer network): Marissa (network diagrams).
- Eviction / suspension playbook (sequence, roles, retention): Karthik (compliance & runbooks).
- Redacted audit logs sample: I will pull a minimal CSV with event IDs and timestamps and redact customer identifiers.

I'll assemble a single zip for your reviewers. A few clarifications before we finalize:

1) For the diagram, do you need the actual VPC subnet CIDRs called out, or just logical flow (we typically provide logical diagrams for external audits)?
2) For the playbook, do you want the human approval chain included, or only the automated steps our runtime executes?

If EOD Tue works for you, we'll target that—I'll include a short narrative that maps each artifact to SIG/C A I Q questions (we'll reference specific control IDs).

—Irene

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / eviction procedures — internal notes

Internal — quick notes before we package:

- Diagram: Produce two layers — a logical lane diagram (control plane, serving pool, customer VPCs, ingress/egress gateways) and a callout view that shows the egress/egress inspection points (NAT/GW + egress deny-by-default). Marissa, can you add a small inset that shows the KV-cache boundary and where cached artifacts are purged during eviction?

- Playbook: We should include these steps:
  1) Detection or request to suspend (security or account ops).
  2) Canary hold: route new traffic to a dedicated holding pool (automated) and drain existing sessions.
  3) Cache purge: KV caches and prefix caches are invalidated for the tenant (runtime automated call).
  4) Data quarantine: ephemeral storage wiped; persistent customer blobs are retained per retention policy but flagged for access review.
  5) Audit and notification: emit structured audit events (eviction.requested, eviction.started, eviction.completed) with correlation ID.

- Logs: Sample will include those three event types. We'll redact PII; keep timestamps and event codes intact so auditors can validate schema.

- Evidence mapping: Map each artifact to SIG v2025-07 control IDs and SOC 2 CC6.1/CC7.1 equivalents.

Jordan — can you double-check the time-to-full-cut SLO we list (we currently say "<= 5 minutes to automated traffic cut, <= 24 hours for complete artifact purge with legal hold exceptions").

Karthik
Director, Compliance Engineering

Attachment: proposed-eviction-timeline.txt

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <sam.park@oakridgehealth.com>
Cc: k arthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / eviction procedures — evidence package (Oakridge)

Samuel — attaching the package for Oakridge review. Summary attached below; full artifacts are in the zip and Drive link. Let me know if you need additional redaction.

Summary (high level):
- Diagram: "tenant-sandboxing-logical.vsdx" (attached) — logical lanes call out control plane (private control plane instance), serving pools (dedicated GPU pools), customer VPC peering, and egress gateways. Inset shows KV cache boundary and cache purge flow.
- Playbook: "redwood-tenant-eviction-playbook-20260814.pdf" (attached) — sequence of automated and manual steps, role matrix, and SLOs. Key SLOs: <=5 minutes for traffic cut; cache invalidation triggered within 60s of eviction.start; artifact purge dependent on legal holds (standard: 24–72h).
- Logs: "sample-audit-logs-2026-08.csv" (attached) — contains three redacted example events: eviction.requested, eviction.started, eviction.completed with correlation IDs and timestamps.

Mappings: Each artifact is annotated to SIG control IDs and SOC 2 CC mappings in the playbook appendix. Drive link and Jira ticket included for traceability.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cTenantSandbox
Jira: SEC-2394

Attachments (in zip): diagram-tenant-sandbox-20260814.vsdx (application/vnd.visio), redwood-tenant-eviction-playbook-20260814.pdf (application/pdf), sample-audit-logs-2026-08.csv (text/csv)

If this looks good I'll also provide a one-page narrative for your board that strips technical callouts and focuses on controls.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
